reasons: No test or other evidence of testing is visible in the code provided.
Conflicts and other save failures are handled and shown to the user.
Some effects suppress React's dependency checks, which can hide stale-value bugs.

terms.meaning: the inputs a component receives from the component that uses it
values a component remembers and updates while the page is open
a request that changes saved data, such as Apply
a version number that goes up each time the deck is saved, used to detect changes made elsewhere
a scripted demo that drives the real screen using local copies instead of saved data
a number that changes each time a new command is sent, so the panel knows to act
a category of filter, such as country or status, shown with counts
a project that is left out of a filter because the number it needs is missing

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared helpers
sections.what: Brings in the tools the panel needs: data saving, icons, the chart builder, the cohort insight and size functions, and the deck types.
sections.why: Reason for the specific imports is clear from the names. The panel reuses shared chart logic so it matches the saved chart.
sections.watch_out: Shared files are reached through long relative paths, so moving this file or the shared folder will break these imports.

sections.name: SIZE_OPTIONS, Range, emptyRange
sections.title: Size choices and range shape
sections.what: Lists the three ways a bubble can be sized: equal, capex and capacity. Also defines the shape of a minimum and maximum filter box, which is kept as text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the inputs produce text, so the values are kept as text until they are needed as numbers.
sections.watch_out: An empty minimum or maximum means no limit, so an empty box is not the same as zero.

sections.name: inRange, sameSet
sections.title: Range check and list comparison
sections.what: Decides whether a project's number falls inside a range. A project with no number gets a missing result rather than being treated as zero. Also compares two lists of choices, ignoring order.
sections.why: Stated in the code: a missing metric is a gap, not zero, so it must not be treated as a real value.
sections.watch_out: Callers must count the missing results separately, because treating them as failures would hide the gap warning.

sections.name: chartSlideIdOf
sections.title: Finding the chart slide
sections.what: Returns the id of the chart slide inside a deck, or nothing if the deck has no chart slide. It uses the shared renderer to decide the id.
sections.why: Stated in the code: the shared renderer decides the id, so the editor and this panel agree on it.
sections.watch_out: If the renderer changes its id scheme, this function finds nothing and the Chart cuts button quietly disappears.

sections.name: ChartCutPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Starting state and choice lists
sections.what: Sets up the panel's inputs and callbacks, loads the saved cut as the starting state, and builds the lists of countries, statuses, technologies, companies and industries. It also decides which sizing options are available based on whether the projects have budgets or capacity figures.
sections.why: Likely reason: the panel opens showing exactly what was last saved, so the user can see and adjust it.
sections.watch_out: A deck with no saved cut counts as showing all projects, and the saved view falls back to delivery, so an older deck can look filtered when it is not.

sections.name: ChartCutPanel: for
sections.title: Filtering projects and building counts
sections.what: Keeps only the projects that match every chosen filter, counting those with missing cost or schedule numbers separately. Also builds the counts shown next to each choice, the chart preview, and the insight sentences.
sections.why: Likely reason: the filtered list drives the preview, the counts and the Apply action from one place.
sections.watch_out: The counts respect the other active filters, so changing one filter can change the numbers next to all the others.

sections.name: ChartCutPanel: if
sections.title: Apply, reset and top controls
sections.what: Applies a prepared replay cut when one arrives, and defines Apply, which saves to the server or to a local copy, and Reset, which clears the filters. It then draws the top status bar, the small-cut warning, the view choices, the missing baseline warning and the sizing buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: Apply and Reset are the two actions that change the saved cut, so they sit with the controls that set it up.
sections.watch_out: Saving sends the deck revision, so if another edit happened first the server returns a conflict and the editor shows a banner rather than overwriting.

sections.name: ChartCutPanel (part 4)
sections.title: Filter chips, ranges and Apply button
sections.what: Draws the bubble size recommendation, the clickable filter chips for industry, technology, company, country and status with their counts, the minimum and maximum boxes for cost and schedule with notes on excluded projects, the insight list, and the Apply button.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the labels. Likely reason: the chips group the filters in a way users can scan quickly.
sections.watch_out: A chip with a zero count stays clickable when it is already selected, so a user can still remove it.

sections.name: ChartCutPanel (part 5)
sections.title: Reset, empty match and error messages
sections.what: Disables Reset when nothing has changed, shows a note when the cut matches no projects, and shows an error with a Retry button when Apply fails for a reason other than a conflict.
sections.why: Likely reason: conflicts are passed to the editor, which shows its own banner, so this panel does not show them twice.
sections.watch_out: Conflicts are hidden here and only shown by the parent banner, so if the parent does not react, a conflict can look like a silent failure.

summary: A panel where the user narrows the projects shown on a scan chart by filters, sizing and view, previews the result, and saves it to the deck or to a local copy.
purpose: Lets the user choose which projects appear in a bubble chart from a finished scan, and see the effect before saving.
why: Likely reason: the chart needs to show a focused group, and the user should see the change before it is saved to the shared deck.
how: 1. Start from the saved cut, with its view, sizing and filters. 2. Let the user change any choice. 3. Keep only projects that match every chosen filter, counting projects with missing cost or schedule data separately. 4. Build a preview of the chart and send it up to the editor. 5. On Apply, save the cut to the deck with its revision number, or apply it to a local copy during a replay. 6. Show warnings for small cuts, missing data and failed saves.
inputs: The saved scan deck with its projects, the saved chart settings, the run id, callbacks from the editor, and in replay mode an optional prepared cut from the demo controller.
outputs: A preview chart sent up to the editor, a saved chart cut sent to the server (or applied to a local copy in replay), and on-screen counts, insights and warnings.
risks: Saving sends the deck revision, so a change made in another tab causes a conflict instead of an overwrite. The panel depends on projects having fields such as cost deviation and schedule overrun, and projects missing them are counted as gaps rather than zero. Some effects suppress dependency warnings, so changes to their inputs can be missed.
debug: If the chart does not match the filters, check the filter loop and the gap counts. If Apply does nothing, check whether the preview is empty, since Apply is disabled without an unsaved change. If saves fail, check the response status: 409 means the deck changed and the editor shows a banner. If a replay preset is ignored, check that the cue nonce changed. If the chart button is missing, check that the shared chart id function finds a chart slide.
